card.name: Linking words in dosing instructions
card.fires_on: Punctuation or small linking words (comma, semicolon, 'and', 'to', 'be') right after an instruction clause about holding, reducing or monitoring a drug. Also the 'ose' in 'Dose' at the start of a sentence.

modes.label: Comma or semicolon after an action
modes.description: A comma or semicolon follows a hold, reduce or interrupt instruction, before the next step.
modes.example: Withhold MEKTOVI for up to 4 weeks<<,>> evaluate LVEF every 2 weeks

modes.label: Linking word inside an instruction
modes.description: A small word like 'to', 'be', 'that' or 'and' sits mid-instruction before a monitoring or follow-up action.
modes.example: The injection should<< be>> completed at the healthcare provider's discretion and

modes.label: Dose at sentence start
modes.description: The 'ose' of 'Dose' opens a sentence about adjustment after a monitoring instruction.
modes.example: Monitor tacrolimus whole blood trough concentrations. D<<ose>> adjustment of tacrolimus may be needed

card.plain: It marks the joints in dosing instructions where the next action, such as monitor or adjust, is about to come.
